newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: HORSE RACING-Australian minister bets on science for Melbourne Cup.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-Australian minister bets on science for Melbourne Cup.

text.p: Australia's science minister has enlisted the aid of the government's peak science agency to tip a winner for the nation's top horse race, the Melbourne Cup.

While ordinary punters are forced to rely on form, or luck, minister Peter McGauran said on Monday mathematics and science tipped Court of Honour as the likely winner of Tuesday's A$2.2 million race -- barring "unforseen events".
McGauran, himself a former amateur jockey, asked mathematics experts at the government's Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation to calculate the likely victor.
The scientists factored in the race distance, fitness of the horses, barrier positions, weight carried and track conditions.

But while declaring confidence in science, McGauran warned his calculations did not take into account the unforseen, "such as nobbling, incompetent riding, pot holes in the track or a monsoonal downpour".
